tagline: Architecture-aware Specs, project understanding, and scoped agents.
title: Concorde Framework

homepage.title: Specify the architecture.
homepage.description: Write and maintain Specs that explain your software’s behavior and architecture. Understand the project through its docsite and Understand Anything graph view. Observe agent execution with LangGraph Studio, guide agents with explicit context and permissions, use built-in agents for development, and track feedback and improvements through the reflection system.

features.title: Specify, understand and improve your software.

items.title: Write and maintain architecture-aware Specs.
items.description: Describe each Module’s purpose, requirements, scenarios and architecture together. Author and review entities, relationships, dependencies and implementation file bindings, and keep the Specs consistent as the software evolves.

items.title: Understand the project. Observe agent execution.
items.description: Browse Specs and architecture diagrams in the docsite, and explore code relationships in the Understand Anything graph view. Follow the agents’ working process with LangGraph Studio: inspect execution graphs and live stage and agent-process events, including starts, completions and failures. Recorded context, permission policies, checks and reviews make the work and its results inspectable.

items.title: Guide agents with Specs and permissions.
items.description: Give each subagent its complete Module Spec and only the file access its phase needs. The host enforces these boundaries. Good results within them increase confidence in the solution, the Spec’s sufficiency and the Modules’ decoupling; tests and review provide further evidence.

items.title: Start with built-in agents.
items.description: A coordinator handles questions, routing and topology design. A Spec engineer authors and reviews Specs, plans work and defines tasks. A programmer implements, reviews and investigates code. Public Skills compose these basic agents into development workflows.

items.title: Turn reflections into tracked improvements.
items.description: Retain project feedback and persistent Spec gaps as records attributed to a Module or scenario. Investigate with scoped access and evidence, preserve developer comments, and turn approved resolutions into fresh development tasks. Records remain available across sessions; developers explicitly decide when to resolve or dismiss them.

workflow.title: Put the Specs to work.
workflow.description: The built-in development loop applies these foundations to a change: update its Module Spec, plan and implement within explicit permissions, then validate and review. Missing contracts and failed checks preserve inspectable progress.

steps.title: Route & specify
steps.description: Select the responsible Module, establish its contract and review the Spec.

steps.title: Plan & implement
steps.description: Turn the contract into tasks, then write code with the declared file access.

steps.title: Validate & review
steps.description: Run configured checks and code review. Bind the resulting evidence to the actual inputs.

steps.title: Ready to deliver
steps.description: Inspect the candidate. Request delivery when ready; request the primary merge separately.

quickstart.title: Start specifying your project.
quickstart.description: Clone and build Concorde, then preview installation into your Git project. Use Python 3.11+, Node.js 18+ and npm; configured checks require Linux with bubblewrap, working namespaces and pidfd support. Choose Codex or Claude and initialize through the installed Skills.
quickstart.code:
git clone https://github.com/FTOD/concorde.git
cd concorde
python3 scripts/concorde.py build

# Replace the path with your Git project.
python3 scripts/install-concorde.py \
  --target /absolute/path/to/project \
  --integration codex --preview

# Review the preview, then rerun with --apply.

reference.title: Agents, capabilities and executable entry points
reference.description: 3 Agents with 12 task modes, 13 capabilities, 8 public Skills and 3 Harnesses. Capabilities orchestrate execution; Agents perform the steps that need model judgment. Public Skills provide instructions for invoking those capabilities from your agent client.

tables.title: Agents and task modes
tables.description: Three Agents provide twelve task modes. Each invocation receives fresh, explicitly bounded context and permissions.
rows: Answer questions, route tasks and design topology from selected complete Module Specs; read-only, with no implementation contents.
specify, context-solve, plan, tasks, spec-review, topology-author
Author and review Specs, assess information sufficiency, and define plans and tasks. Returns structured results; the host applies document changes.
Implement tasks, review code and investigate problems. Only implementation may write the selected Module's implementation files.

tables.title: Capability inventory
tables.description: Four lifecycle capabilities make no model calls; the other nine may call a model. Eight public Skills each expose one global or lifecycle capability. The five stages run only through declared host composition. Current Agents have no admitted Capability references of their own; the host composes workflows.
rows: Answer questions, route requests, and design and apply accepted topology changes.
Route a change through specification, planning, implementation, validation and review to a ready candidate.
Run a standalone Spec or code review, including source diagnosis.
Inspect feedback, capture gaps, investigate, implement resolutions and manage owned records.
Propose and apply project initialization with a pinned Protocol.
Run deterministic Spec and configured code checks and record readiness.
Stage a verified candidate on its own branch and clean up; merge into the primary branch on a separate explicit request.
Author Spec replacements for the bound Module.
Validate Module participant routing and assess context sufficiency.
Assess sufficiency and produce a revision-bound plan.
Derive acceptance tasks from the accepted plan.
Implement component tasks or coordinate participating components.

tables.title: Harnesses and native tools
tables.description: All three Harnesses declare native.filesystem and native.shell Tool interfaces and support Codex and Claude. The Harness and mode define authority ceilings; the host grants concrete access for each invocation.
rows: Project implementation workspace with access restricted by the selected mode and host grant.

tables.title: Launchers and supporting tools
tables.description: Commands are relative to the source checkout. Installed projects use the corresponding scripts under .concorde/framework/; Studio and development setup are documented separately. CLI validate performs direct validation; concorde-validate also manages candidate readiness evidence. Studio uses the same host and capabilities as the CLI and Skills.
rows: Invoke one of the eight public capabilities using a typed JSON request, in execute or describe-policy mode.
Start, observe and debug the same eight public workflows through the shared CapabilityHost.
Preview or apply installation into a project.
Query and maintain the reflection queue.
start, build, validate, typecheck, test, check.
Explain or check the source-checkout worktree policy.
